_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Operational Test Program Instruction/Test Program Instruction (OTPI/TPI)
summary: Specifies the format and content requirements for an Operational Test Program Instruction/Test Program Instruction (OTPI/TPI), which provides connection instructions and data used to troubleshoot elements of an Operational Test Program Set (OTPS).
use_relationship:
An Operational Test Program Set (OTPS) is a collection of hardware, software and data to test Avionics items (all from the same Aircraft or Weapons System) of similar characteristics and functions. By grouping these Avionics items, the hardware, software and data needed by Automatic Test System operators is minimized.

The OTPI is a collection of TPIs that share this hardware, software and data. The TPIs provide connection instructions and data used to trouble-shoot the individual elements of the OTPS.

This DID supersedes DI-TMSS-81760.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Reference document
preparation_instructions.content: The applicable issue of the documents cited herein, including their approval dates and dates of any applicable amendments, notices, and revisions, shall be as specified in the contract.

preparation_instructions.title: General
preparation_instructions.content: The Operational Test Program Instruction/Test Program Instruction (OTPI/TPI) specified herein shall be in a digital form.

preparation_instructions.title: Format
preparation_instructions.content: The OTPI/TPI shall conform to the general guidelines for planning and preparation of the Work Package (WP) concept defined in NAVAIR 00-25-700 as applied to the TPI contents contained herein.

children.title: Page layout
children.content: The OTPI/TPI shall consist of all text pages including tabular data and illustrations in a form suitable for display on a computer screen. Text shall be single column single spaced, with a left justified margin. Text shall be double spaced between paragraphs, procedural steps, and before and after warnings, cautions, and notes.

children.title: Margins
children.content: (see figure 1.) All page margins, including title/cover pages must have a left margin of one inch and a right margin of one-half inch. Top and bottom margins shall be one-half inch.

children.title: Page size
children.content: (see figure 1.) Page sizes shall be limited to two sizes:

children.title: 8 1/2 inches (width) by 11 inches (length)
17 inches (width) by 11 inches (length)
Text image area
Page size 8 1/2 x 11 inches
children.content: The text and illustration image area is 7 inches wide and 10 inches high.

children.title: Page size 17 x 11 inches
children.content: The text and illustration image area in 15 1/4 inches wide and 10 inches in length.

children.title: Type Size
children.content: The text type size for all OTPIs/TPIs shall have a minimum typeface of 8 points and a maximum of 12 points.

children.title: Indentation
children.content: Indentation shall be consistent with paragraph 3.2.5.

children.title: Numbering
OTPI Number
children.content: Each OTPI number shall be assigned a permanent number in accordance with the contract.

children.title: TPI number
children.content: Each TPI number shall be assigned a permanent number in accordance with the contract.

children.title: Work package number
children.content: Each TPI work package (WP) number shall be assigned as specified herein (see 3.5 below).

children.title: Page numbers
children.content: Pages shall be numbered consecutively within each WP using Arabic numerals beginning with the number one. On WP title pages, the page number and count shall be placed below the WP number in 10- to 12-point bold type right justified with the WP number; for example, "Page 1 of 20." On second and subsequent WP pages, only the page number shall appear.

children.title: Paragraph numbers
children.content: TPI paragraphs shall be numbered as follows:

children.title: Paragraph and subparagraph divisions
children.content:
Paragraph and subparagraph divisions shall be numbered consecutively for every field of information. Paragraphs within a WP having subparagraphs shall be numbered consecutively by a decimal numbering system as follows:

1. PRIMARY PARAGRAPH
1.1 SECONDARY SUBPARAGRAPH
1.1.1 Tertiary Subparagraph
1.1.1.1 Quaternary subparagraph

children.title: Introductory matter and technical content text
children.content: Introductory matter and technical content text shall contain one or more main paragraphs which may be divided into subordinate paragraphs. Major paragraphs shall have a brief underlined heading describing the content or action portrayed.

children.title: For clarity, paragraph numbering should be limited
children.content: For clarity, paragraph numbering should be limited to three sub-levels unless additional sub-levels are unavoidable.

children.title: Illustrations and table numbers
children.content: Illustrations and tables within a WP shall be numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals beginning with the number one.

children.title: Illustrations
children.content: Each sheet of a multi-sheet illustration shall be identified by a sheet number following the figure number and title below the illustration. Each sheet shall include the total number of sheets that make up the figure; for example, "Figure 2. Inertial Sensor Element Assembly Test Diagram (Sheet 1 of 5)." Remaining sheets shall be numbered in consecutive order, Sheet 2 of 5, Sheet 3 of 5, and so forth.

children.title: Tables
children.content: Each table shall be identified by a table number and an underlined title above the table. Each sheet of a multi-sheet table shall include the total number of sheets that make up the table; for example, "Table 2. Command message data content. (Sheet 1 of 5)". Remaining sheets shall be numbered in consecutive order, Sheet 2 of 5, Sheet 3 of 5, and so forth.

children.title: Blank page numbers
children.content: A Blank page shall be assigned a number, but it shall appear on the preceding page; e.g., if page 10 is blank, page 9 shall bear the number "9/ (10 blank)." Alternatively, the numbered page is annotated "This page intentionally left blank."

children.title: Warnings, cautions, and notes
children.content: Warnings, cautions, and notes shall be used to introduce items of information which are parenthetical (cannot logically be included in the text) and which the writer feels must be emphasized. A warning or caution shall immediately precede the text to which it refers.

children.title: Use of symbols
children.content: The symbols should be used sparingly, consistent with real need. Titles are identified by the following labeling:

children.title: Warning
children.content: The warning title shall be capitalized with a 1-point rule above and below the title.

children.title: Caution
children.content: The caution title shall be capitalized with a 1-point rule below the title.

children.title: Note
children.content: The note title shall be capitalized.

children.title: Headings and text
children.content: Warning, caution and note headings shall precede the text to which they apply. The text shall not contain procedural steps, direct maintenance actions, or be numbered. Warnings and cautions may be worded positively or negatively and shall state the hazard and result or reason for the instruction or the consequences if not heeded, unless obvious.

children.title: Placement
children.content: The title shall be in the horizontal center of the page. None of the three are ever plural (i.e., "NOTES" is not acceptable). The text of a warning, caution, or note is centered horizontally under its title. If several distinct items of information are to be covered at the same time and all are of the same type (i.e., more than one warning, caution, or note), include all under the single appropriate heading, number each item and double space between items. Avoid having cautions, warning or notes follow each other consecutively without intervening text. The text of warnings, cautions, or notes shall not be divided at the end of a page.

children.title: Use of warnings, cautions, and notes
Warning
children.content: Use a warning for information which, if not regarded might result in injury to personnel.

children.title: Caution
children.content: Use a caution for information which, if not regarded, might result in damage to equipment.

children.title: Note
children.content: Use a note for information which is too bulky to be included internally within parentheses. In most instances, a note should immediately follow the text to which it refers, but it may precede if the context demands. For example, in text procedures, it may be desirable to tell the reader that if certain conditions are met, then certain succeeding steps can be omitted. A figure note has an initial capital and is not underscored.

children.title: Use of abbreviations, acronyms, and terms
children.content: Individual words and word combinations can only be abbreviated when their meaning is unquestionably clear. When in doubt, the word(s) must be spelled out.

children.title: Work package numbering system
children.content: Each WP shall be assigned a permanent number in accordance with 5. below.

children.title: Work package number assignment
children.content: Each WP number shall have a five digit number, beginning with the number WP 001 00. There shall be one blank space between the third and fourth numerals.

children.title: Assignment of the last two digits of the work package number
children.content: The last two digits of any WP number may be assigned by the developer/contractor in the basic issue and by the cognizant activity in any change cycle following distribution of the basic issue.

preparation_instructions.title: OTPI
preparation_instructions.content: The OTPI consists of front matter and, if applicable, common technical WPs.

children.title: OTPI Front Matter
children.content:
Front Matter consists of the following (see figure 9):
OTPI Title Page
OTPI Master Index of TPIs (normally page 2)
OTPI Record of Revisions/Changes (normally page 3)

children.title: OTPI Title page
children.content: (see figure 2.) A title page shall serve as the cover for the OTPI. The title page shall provide sufficient information to correlate the OTPI to the Operational Test program Set (OTPS) and include the following:

children.title: The OTPI number shall be placed in the upper left corner
children.content: The OTPI number shall be placed in the upper left corner of the page. Each manual or volume shall have a separate number assigned. The OTPI number shall be in 18- to 20-point bold type.

children.title: A 1-point rule shall be placed 1 1/2 inches from the top
children.content: A 1-point rule shall be placed 1 1/2 inches from the top of the page below the OTPI number.

children.title: The title "OPERATIONAL TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION" shall be centered
children.content: The title "OPERATIONAL TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION" shall be centered on the page below the 1-point rule, in 16- to 18-point type.

children.title: The words "FOR TESTING." shall be centered below the title
children.content: The words "FOR TESTING." in 12- to 14-point type, shall be centered below the words "OPERATIONAL TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION" with the aircraft type/model/series centered below, both in 14- to 16-point bold type.

children.title: The aircraft system nomenclature being tested and model number
children.content: The aircraft system nomenclature being tested and model number; for example, 'STANDARD ATTITUDE READING REFERENCE SYSTEM (SAHRS) AN/USN-2(V)' shall be centered below the aircraft type, in 16- to 18-point bold type.

children.title: The word 'USING' shall be centered below the aircraft system/model number
children.content: The word 'USING' in 12- to 14-point type, shall be centered below the aircraft system/model number with the "AN" identification of the Automatic Test Equipment (ATE) test system, name and acronym (if any) of the test system, in 14- to 16-point type.

children.title: Centered below the test system shall be the developing activity and contract number
children.content: Centered below the test system shall be the developing activity and contract number, in 10- to 12-point type.

children.title: The contract-specified distribution statement and warning statement
children.content: The contract-specified distribution statement and warning statement, as identified in the Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL), shall be left-justified below the developing activity and contract number in 10 pt. type. The words "DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT X." (where "X" is the contract-specified distribution statement letter) shall start the distribution statement and shall be bold and underlined. The word "WARNING - " shall start the warning notice and shall be bold and underlined.

children.title: The contract-specified destruction notice
children.content: The contract-specified destruction notice, as identified in the Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL), shall be left-justified below the distribution and warning statements in 10 pt. type. The words "DESTRUCTION NOTICE - " shall start the destruction notice and shall be bold and underlined.

children.title: A 1-point rule shall be placed 1 1/2 inches above the bottom of the page
The OTPI date shall be placed in the lower right corner
children.content: The OTPI date shall be placed in the lower right corner, above the 1-point ruler in 10- to 12-point type.

children.title: The change number shall be placed above the OTPI date
children.content: The change number shall be placed above the OTPI date, in 10- to 12-point type.

children.title: OTPI Master Index
children.content: (see figure 3.) The OTPI Master Index shall contain an index of TPIs for the entire manual. The index pages shall immediately follow the title page and always start on page two of the OTPI and include the following:

children.title: The OTPI publication number shall be placed in the upper left corner
children.content: The OTPI publication number shall be placed in the upper left corner of the page, in 14- to 16-point bold type.

children.title: The page identification shall be placed in the upper right corner
children.content: The page identification (Page 2, Page 3, etc.) shall be placed in the upper right corner of the page, in 10- to 12-point bold type.

children.title: The title "MASTER INDEX OF TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTIONS" shall be centered
children.content: The title "MASTER INDEX OF TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTIONS" shall be centered, in 12- to 14-point bold type.

children.title: Column heads shall be placed below the title
children.content: Column heads "TPI Number," "Title," "Volume Number" (if applicable), and "Change Number" shall be placed below the title. A 1-point rule shall be placed above and below the column heads.

children.title: A linked and/or hyperlinked numerical listing of TPIs
children.content: A linked and/or hyperlinked numerical listing of TPIs and common WPs assigned to the manual and the numbers, titles, volumes numbers (if applicable), and change number shall be placed below the applicable column heads.

children.title: OTPI Record of revisions and changes (REVCHG)
children.content: (see figure 4.) A list of revisions/changes incorporated shall be specified for all manuals. This page shall begin with the original issue of the OTPI coinciding with the delivery of the OTPS and subsequently maintained by the cognizant activity to list all subsequent revisions and changes. The REVCHG page(s) shall follow the index page and include the following:

children.title: The OTPI publication number shall be placed in the upper left corner
children.content: The OTPI publication number shall be placed in the upper left corner of the page, in 16 point bold type.

children.title: The page identification shall be placed in the upper right corner
children.content: The page identification (Page 3, Page 4, etc.) shall be placed in the upper right corner of the page on the same line as the OTPI publication number in 16 pt bold type.

children.title: The OTPI date or revision date shall be in the upper left corner
children.content: The OTPI date or revision date shall be in the upper left corner below the publication number in 10- to 12-point type.

children.title: The title "OPERATIONAL TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION, RECORD OF REVISIONS/CHANGES" shall be centered
children.content: The title "OPERATIONAL TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION, RECORD OF REVISIONS/CHANGES" shall be centered on the page below the publication number, in 12- to 14-point type, split into 2 lines at the comma.

children.title: The original issue date must be included
children.content: The original issue date must be included and labeled "ORIGINAL ISSUE" with an appropriate date below title, in 10- to 12-point type.

children.title: The page shall be in column format
children.content: The page shall be in column format with column heads TPI No,." REVCHG No.." "DATE," and "REASON FOR CHANGE." A 1-point rule shall be placed above and below the column heads.

children.title: OTPI Common Technical WPs
children.content:
A technical content WP is considered common if it is applicable to more than one TPI in an OTPI. A common technical WP shall take the publication number of the OTPI.

Common technical WPs are generally self-contained PDF files and include:
WP 002 02 System Wiring Diagram

and, if applicable:
WP 003 02 Common Test Program Source Listing, and
WP 003 04 Common Digital Test Program Source Listing.

These files are accessed via hyperlinks from OTPI and TPI indexes.

children.title: OTPI WP 002 02 System Wiring Diagram (SWD)
children.content: The SWD is a diagram that shows all wiring and hardware devices between the Unit Under Test (UUT) and the ATE. The diagram shall show the "as-built", not the electrical equivalence of the wiring and hardware devices. See paragraph 5.2.1.4 for a detailed SWD description.

children.title: OTPI WP 003 02 Common Source Listing
children.content:
Consists of formatted WP data per 5.2.1 immediately followed by a hyperlinked list of Source Code filenames (*.LU, *.AS and any others as appropriate) and procedure names.

Each filename hyperlink shall connect to the beginning of the referenced file listing. Each procedure name hyperlink shall link to the particular common Source Code procedure.

children.title: OTPI WP 003 04 Common Digital Source Listing
children.content:
Consists of formatted WP data per 5.2.1 immediately followed by a hyperlinked list of common Digital Source filenames (*.PMP, *.SYM and any others as appropriate) and procedure names.

Each filename hyperlink shall connect to the beginning of the referenced file listing. Each procedure name hyperlink shall link to the particular Digital Source routine.

children.title: OTPI/TPI security classification
children.content: The classification of the OTPI/TPI shall be as defined in the Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL).

preparation_instructions.title: TPI
preparation_instructions.content:
The TPI consists of front matter and technical content WPs. (see figure 9):

Front Matter
Title Page
TPI Numerical Index of Work Packages (normally Page 2),
Revisions/Changes (normally page 3), and
if applicable, List of peculiar Abbreviations/Acronyms used.

Technical Content WPs
WP 001 00 Supplemental Testing Data
Optional: contains messages and/or graphics that are too complex for display by the TPS.

WP 002 00 Test Diagnostic Information
WP 002 01 Test Oriented Wire List (TOWL).
hyperlink to OTPI WP 002 02 System Wiring Diagram.

WP 003 00 Program source code information
WP 003 01 Program source code.
(hyperlink to OTPI WP 003 02 Common source listing.)
WP 003 03 Digital Test program source listing.
(hyperlink to OTPI WP 003 04 Common digital source listing.)
WP 003 05+ Additional sub-WPs to accommodate other TPS source modules as applicable.

children.title: TPI front matter
TPI title page
children.content: (see figure 5.) The TPI title page shall include the following:

children.title: The title page shall indicate the TPI publication number
children.content: The title page shall indicate the TPI publication number in the upper left corner of the page, in 16- to 18-point bold type.

children.title: A 1-point rule shall be placed 1 1/2 inches from the top
children.content: A 1-point rule shall be placed 1 1/2 inches from the top of the page below the TPI number.

children.title: The title "TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION" shall be centered
children.content: The title "TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION" shall be centered on the page below the 1-point rule, in 14- to 16-point bold type.

children.title: The words "FOR TESTING," shall be centered below the title
children.content: The words "FOR TESTING," in 12- to 14-point type, shall be centered below the words "TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION" with the UUT nomenclature and part number centered below, both in 16- to 18-point bold type.

children.title: The word "USING" shall be centered below the UUT nomenclature
children.content: The word "USING" shall be centered below the UUT nomenclature with the "AN" identification of the ATE test system, name and acronym (if any) of the test system, in 10- to 12-point type.

children.title: The words "PART OF" shall be placed in the lower left corner
children.content: The words "PART OF" shall be placed in the lower left corner above the 1-point rule with the OTPI publication number and date identified, in 10- to 12-point type.

children.title: A 1-point rule shall be placed 1 1/2 inches above the bottom of the page
The TPI change no. and date shall be placed in the lower right corner
children.content: The TPI change no. and date shall be placed in the lower right corner, above the 1-point rule, in 10- to 12-point type.

children.title: TPI numerical index of work packages
children.content: (see figure 6.) The TPI numerical index of Work Packages shall contain a hyperlinked index of WPs for the TPI. The index page shall immediately follow the title page and normally begin on page 2 of the TPI and include the following:

children.title: The TPI publication number shall be placed in the upper left corner
children.content: The TPI publication number shall be placed in the upper left corner of the page, in 14- to 16-point bold type.

children.title: The page identification shall be placed in the upper right corner
children.content: The page identification (normally, Page 2) shall be placed in the upper right corner of the page on the same line as the publication number, in 16 pt. bold type.

children.title: The title "TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION" shall be entered
children.content: The title "TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION" shall be entered in 14- to 16-point bold type.

children.title: The title "NUMERICAL INDEX OF WORK PACKAGES" shall be centered
children.content: The title "NUMERICAL INDEX OF WORK PACKAGES" shall be centered, in 12- to 14-point type.

children.title: Centered below the title shall be the words "WORK PACKAGE INDEX"
children.content: Centered below the title shall be the words "WORK PACKAGE INDEX" with column heads "WP NO., "TITLE," and "CHANGE NO." below. A 1-point rule shall be placed above and below the column headings.

children.title: A numerical listing of WPs assigned to the manual
children.content: A numerical listing of WPs assigned to the manual and their titles shall be placed below the applicable column heads.

children.title: The TPI change date shall be placed below the title
children.content: The TPI change date shall be placed below the title in 10- to 12-point type.

children.title: Revisions/changes
children.content: (see figure 7.) A list of revisions/changes incorporated shall be specified for all manuals. This page shall begin with the original issue of the OTPI/TPI coinciding with the delivery of the OTPS and subsequently maintained by the cognizant activity to list all subsequent revisions and changes. The WP REVCHG page shall follow the WP index page and include the following:

children.title: The TPI publication number shall be placed in the upper left corner
children.content: The TPI publication number shall be placed in the upper left corner of the page, in 14- to 16-point bold type.

children.title: The TPI date or revision date shall be in the upper left corner
children.content: The TPI date or revision date shall be in the upper left corner below the publication number in 10- to 12-point type.

children.title: The page identification shall be placed in the upper right corner
children.content: The page identification (Page 3, Page 4, etc.) shall be placed in the upper right corner, on the same line and in the same font as the publication number right justified.

children.title: The title "TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION RECORD OF REVISIONS/CHANGES" shall be centered
children.content: The title "TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION RECORD OF REVISIONS/CHANGES" shall be centered on the page below the publication number, in 12- to 14-point type.

children.title: The page shall be in column format
children.content: The page shall be in column format with column heads "REVCHG NO.," "DATE," "REASON FOR CHANGE," and "TPI/WP AFFECTED (PARA., TABLE, FIGURE, etc.)," in 12-point type. A 1-point rule shall be placed above and below the column heads.

children.title: A list of current changes assigned to the manual
children.content: A list of current changes assigned to the manual shall be placed below the applicable column heads.

children.title: Technical-content work package
children.content: All WPs numbered WP 001 00 and above shall be considered technical content WPs.

children.title: Technical content package title page
children.content: (see figure 8.) The title page shall include the following:

children.title: The OTPI or TPI publication number shall be placed
children.content: The OTPI or TPI (as applicable) publication number shall be placed in the upper left corner of the page in 14- to 16-point bold type.

children.title: The work package number shall be placed in the upper right hand corner
children.content: The work package number shall be placed in the upper right hand corner on the same line as the publication number, in 14- to 16-point bold type.

children.title: The WP change number and date shall be placed below the publication number
children.content: The WP change number and date shall be placed below the publication number in 12 pt. type. The page number and number of pages shall be placed below the WP number in 12 to 14 point type.

children.title: A 1-point rule shall be placed 1 1/2 inches from the top
children.content: A 1-point rule shall be placed 1 1/2 inches from the top of the page below the TPI number.

children.title: The words "OPERATIONAL TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION" or "TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION"
children.content: The words "OPERATIONAL TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION" or "TEST PROGRAM INSTRUCTION", as applicable, followed by the technical contents (i.e. title) of the WP shall be centered on the page in 12 to 14 point. bold type.

children.title: The words "FOR TESTING" shall be centered below the contents title
children.content: For TPI WPs, the following apply: The words "FOR TESTING" in 12, to 14-point type shall be centered below the contents title with the UUT nomenclature an number centered below, both in 14- to 16-point bold type.

children.title: A 1-point rule shall be placed below the technical contents title
TPI WP 001 00 Supplemental Testing Data
children.content:
Work Package 001 00 will convey to the TPS operator any required data to successfully run the UUT or self-test TPS that is not available in any other TPS documentation including TPS output messages, MTPSI, and Technical Manuals for the UUT and/or Operational Test Program Hardware (OTPH).

If included, WP 001 00 shall contain:

children.title: Format WP data per 5.2.1 above
WP 001 00 may include the following paragraphs
children.content:
WP 001 00 may include the following paragraphs, or any others deemed applicable within the constraints of this WP.

1. UNTESTED HARDWARE
2. SELECT AT TEST PROCEDURE
3. OTHER MESSAGES (Any other messages too wordy or complex to be put in the TPS program)

If no supplemental testing data is required, the TPI will contain a WP 001 00. The first page of the formatted WP shall state "This Work Package Intentionally Omitted"

children.title: TPI WP 002 00 Test Diagnostic Information (TDI)
children.content:
The TDI consists of two parts. Part 1 is a Test Oriented Wire List (TOWL) of active wire segments used during a particular test. Part 2 is a System Wiring Diagram (SWD) of the entire OTPH. WP 002 00 will contain a description of the use of the TOWL in conjunction with the SWD and links to TPI WP 002 01 TOWL and OTPI WP 002 02 SWD.

NOTE: TOWL and SWD samples can be found at both web sites listed below: https://pma260.navair.navy.mil or http://www.acq.osd.mil.

children.title: TPI WP 002 01 Test Oriented Wire List
children.content:
The TOWL is a list of the point-to-point connections of wire segments within the OTPH. Each wire segment is prefaced with an abbreviation to indicate its whereabouts within the ATE, the OTPH or the UUT (e.g. GPI:P9-11B to ID:TB0610-F indicates the wire of interest has one end at the GPI panel and the other inside the OTPH on TB0610). For complex OTPH that has an interface device that contains terminal blocks, as well as a test fixture with terminal blocks then TF:TB0610-F would indicate that the terminal block is in the test fixture, not the interface device. The first page of WP 002 01 will contain an index for all test numbers with links to the TOWL point-to-point wire segment connections for each test.

The TOWL shall be prepared in a tabular format with five column headings as follows

ASSET Identifies the asset (ATE, GPETE, ancillary, etc.) providing the measurement/stimulus
FROM Identifies the connector/pin reference for the signal path segment
TO Identifies the ending connector/pin reference for the signal path segment
FROM SHEET Identifies the SWD sheet where the connector reference can be located
TO SHEET Identifies the SWD sheet where the "to" connector reference can be located

Bold green text shall be used to identify previously unchecked paths. Regular green text shall identify checked paths. An asterisk "*" shall be placed next to the wire path in the TOWL to indicate a daisy chained path. The "FROM" and "TO" path shall be linked to allow direct opening of the corresponding schematic PDF that is part of the System Wiring Diagram. Wire paths in the TOWL that have not been checked by a previous test shall be identified by bold red text. Wire paths in the TOWL that have been checked by previous tests shall be identified by regular underlined blue text. An exclamation point "!" shall be placed next to the wire path in the TOWL to indicate a path that is not directly used by this test but is connected to the test path.

The listing shall follow an orderly flow that matches the flow of the SWD. A wire segment in the SWD may begin on one sheet and end on another. The TOWL shall include sheet numbers for both the "from" and "to" pins. When a listed pin is part of ATE, the asset name (from CASS .RTT, for instance) is included on that line. When a listed pin is part of the UUT, then "UUT" is added to that line. The Source Code header commentary for each test shall be included as part of the TOWL to provide the operator insight into the test functionality.

See figure 10 for a presentation example.

children.title: OTPI WP 002 02 System Wiring Diagram (SWD)
children.content: SWD shall be prepared in accordance with ASME Y14.24-1999, paragraph 10.3. Symbolic representation of all OTPH electrical components shall be in accordance with ASME Y14.24-1999, Paragraph 10.3.3. A wire list shall NOT be substituted for any portion of the SWD. The SWD shall provide an explicit illustration between the ATE, OTPH and UUT. The SWD shall be developed to print on 11" X 17" paper size (B size drawings). All font sizes shall be a minimum of 8 point. When more than one sheet is required to describe a SWD, the SWD shall be clearly identified with appropriate notation on all associated SWD sheets as to the total number of sheets (i.e. sheet 1 of 38). The SWD shall show all hardware elements of the OTPH containing circuitry/wiring (i.e. Splice Points, Terminal Blocks, mother boards, CCA schematic etc.) including all repairable and non-repairable assemblies etc. as well as the ATE (CASS) assets used (i.e. instruments, station relays). The following information is provided to ensure standardization:

children.title: The front page of the SWD shall have all terms and definitions
children.content: The front page of the SWD shall have all terms and definitions used in the SWD identified.

children.title: For OTPH designed for use on CASS ATE
children.content: For OTPH designed for use on CASS ATE: CASS assets are identified with the GPI: label. Instruments are further identified with their RTT labels.

children.title: All ATE asset blocks are drawn with bold lines
children.content: All ATE asset blocks are drawn with bold lines to differentiate the OTPH hardware from the ATE hardware.

children.title: The SWD shall include all ATE assets used by the TPS
children.content: The SWD shall include all ATE assets used by the TPS including RF, EO and ancillary assets such as the ADTS, MPSRD, VPG, ULAS, BTI, EO Cart, etc.

children.title: All labels used in the SWD and TOWL shall match
children.content: All labels used in the SWD and TOWL shall match. Examples of labeling are: GPI:P9, ID:TB3_11, and MB:J10.

children.title: Relays shall show all NO/NC designations
children.content: Relays shall show all NO/NC designations. ATE relay identification numbers are not required.

children.title: Unused pins that are identified on the SWD
children.content: Unused pins that are identified on the SWD shall be annotated with NC (no connection). Alternatively, unused pins may have an "X" placed at the open termination.

children.title: Wire connections such as splice points
children.content: Wire connections such as splice points shall be identified with a standard tie point or "dot".

children.title: The SWD portion of the TDI is a point-to-point representation
children.content:
The SWD portion of the TDI is a point-to-point representation of the OTPH as built. That is, wire segments are clearly delineated. Refer to Example 1.

In View 1, pins A and D each hold one wire, while pins B and C each hold two.

In View 2, pins A and B each hold one wire, while pins C and D each hold two.

In View 3, pins A, B, C and D each hold one wire and all of the other ends are terminated in a splice.

All three views are electrically identical, but quite different for the technician trying to trace wires through an OTPH. The point of the SWD is to provide an accurate tracing of wire segments through an OTPH.

children.title: Splice points shall be referred to as SP
children.content: Splice points shall be referred to as "SP".

children.title: TPI WP 003 00 Source Code Test Information and Index
children.content: Consists of formatted WP data 5.2.1 above and the following two paragraphs:

children.title: Paragraph 1, SOURCE CODE TEST INFORMATION
children.content: Paragraph 1, SOURCE CODE TEST INFORMATION, is a description of the content of each sub-WP.

children.title: Paragraph 1.1, SOURCE CODE TEST INDEX
children.content:
Paragraph 1.1, SOURCE CODE TEST INDEX, is hyperlinked listing of the sub-WP numbers and titles.

The index shall list and provide links and/or hyperlinks to all applicable Source Code modules including OTPI WPs 003 02 and/or 003 04, if applicable.

children.title: TPI WP 003 01 Test Program Source Listing
children.content:
Consists of formatted WP data per 5.2.1 above, immediately followed by a hyperlinked list of Source Code filenames (*.LU, *.AS and any others as appropriate) and Source Code test numbers.

Each filename hyperlink shall connect to the beginning of the referenced file listing. Each test number hyperlink shall connect to the program source code for that test number.

children.title: OTPI WP 003 02 Common Source Listing
children.content: Source code that is common to multiple TPSs within the OTPS shall be provided in OTPI WP 003 02, see 4.5 above.

children.title: TPI WP 003 03 Digital Program Source Listing
children.content:
If applicable, consists of formatted WP data per 5.2.1 immediately followed by a hyperlinked list of TPS-specific digital filenames (*.PMP, *.SYM and any others as appropriate) and procedure names.

Each filename hyperlink shall connect to the beginning of the referenced file listing. Each procedure name hyperlink shall link to the particular Digital Source routine.

children.title: OTPI WP 003 04 Common Digital Source Listing
children.content: Digital Source code that is common to multiple TPSs within the OTPS shall be provided in OTPI WP 003 04, see 4.6 above.

children.title: TPI WP 003 05+ Additional TPS Source Listings
children.content: Additional TPS source module listings, if required.
